survey: A round analog clock with a thick orange rim and a white face. It stands upright on the floor of a shallow green striped alcove. The bottom of the rim touches the ground and a contact shadow sits under it. The camera is slightly off-axis, so the face reads as a gentle ellipse and the rim looks a little deeper on the left, which is consistent perspective. The face has 12 navy hour marks, with the 2 o'clock mark hidden under the tip of the minute hand, and minute dots between the marks. Three hands share one navy center cap: the hour hand points at about 10, the minute hand at 2 (a correct 10:10 reading), and a thin red second hand points toward about 7 with a short tail past the hub. Every hand comes from the center pivot, the rim encloses the face cleanly, the clock rests on the surface, and nothing floats or is invented.
